correctness.rationale: Exact inversion yields the disjoint two-branch IFS, a monotone derivative maximum and the unique sharp cubic root; elementary contraction gives shift coding and repelling periodic points retained in the interval. Uniform log-derivative distortion proves the survival quasi-multiplicative inequality and hence the strictly positive escape exponent. Sharp derivative sum bounds give the escape logarithm(mu/3) plus O(1/mu). Cylinder upper covers, a Bernoulli Frostman lower bound and the direct exponential-volume cover establish 0<dimension<1 and its three-term logarithmic expansion. The decoded package checker passed 500 independent 85-digit inversions and the exact-rational discriminant identity. Outside-excursion periodic points are not counted.

originality.rationale: Full primary works and four exact-same-map published theorem texts were compared by parameter domain and implication. The original 2022 article and the 2025 interpolation treat fixed-point/numerical bifurcations; the other four results prove low-gain period-two/three statements on the invariant interval. None implies the specified above-threshold Cantor escape and dimension asymptotics. Generic IFS coding/distortion is explicitly credited as background. Residual risk: an unlocated paper may have already specialized cookie-cutter methods to this exact high-gain rational map.
residual_risks: There may be older or unindexed work applying generic expanding-Cantor-set theory to exactly this rational family and deriving the same asymptotic coefficients.
The 2024 deformed K-map article was available only partially; its accessible subject is numerical q-deformed dynamics, but exact high-gain overlap cannot be ruled out solely from the abstract.
The threshold mu_h characterizes uniform one-step contraction, not a necessarily sharp onset of hyperbolicity of the full survivor.

value.rationale: Above mu=3+2 sqrt2 the original dynamical map no longer preserves its modeling interval, making survivor dynamics a natural missing global question. The proof supplies a sharp explicit one-step hyperbolicity threshold, an all-time survival-rate bound and map-specific escape and three-term dimension asymptotics; these quantify survival rather than merely renaming classical Cantor coding, and motivate applications to postcritical escape statistics. No external application performance is asserted.
